stories.journey: Any local client discovers or starts one authenticated per-user/data-directory daemon with version negotiation, then attaches instead of forking a second owner. Covers audit gap 1 (no default installed-app journey) and AUD-001 missing auth/singleton findings.
tests: Twenty concurrent launches in a disposable HOME produce one daemon and one database owner; the rest attach.
Forged, stale-PID, symlinked or other-user descriptors cannot redirect credentials or authorize a server.
Health/version negotiation rejects a mismatched daemon with an actionable error and no infinite retry.
An occupied port or reused PID never causes an unrelated process to be killed.
Stop/restart rotates or preserves credentials by explicit policy and existing clients reconnect safely.
stories.title: Daemon authenticated discovery, startup and recovery

stories.journey: The installed opencode2 binary exposes the full upstream command surface with no subcommand opening the real application. Covers AUD-001 install-path inventory finding and the opencode-rk binary-name divergence.
tests: opencode2 with no subcommand discovers/starts the daemon and opens the native TUI without manual serve or session setup.
The installed command list matches the upstream packages/cli surface or records an approved deviation per command.
Installed artifacts identify as opencode2; the opencode-rk name appears nowhere in packaged output.
Install scripts exist with checksums for every supported platform and fail closed on an unknown target.
An unknown subcommand prints actionable help and exits nonzero without starting a daemon.
stories.title: Installed opencode2 command inventory and binary identity

stories.journey: Every registered native tool dispatches through the executor, policy broker, session state and durable output chain. Covers the AUD-005 register-without-dispatch unwired finding.
tests: Each registered tool invoked through the registry executes via executor, policy, state and durable output.
An unknown tool name returns a typed error with no side effects and no spawned process.
Concurrent dispatches respect bounded permits and never exceed the configured parallelism.
Every dispatch records a durable tool call/result pair with timestamps and request provenance.
Cancelling a dispatch reclaims its task and leaves no orphan process or held permit.
stories.title: Native tool registry dispatch wiring

stories.journey: Shell and file tools enforce authorization, timeouts, cancellation and byte budgets before and during execution. Covers AUD-005 shell timeout/cancel/bounds and permission deny-no-side-effect repair items.
tests: An unauthorized shell command is denied with no spawned process and a durable denial event.
A runaway command is killed at its timeout and reports truncated bounded output with an explicit marker.
Cancel during execution reaches a stable cancelled state with no leaked child process.
Output beyond the byte budget truncates with an explicit marker and never grows the buffer unboundedly.
A denied file write leaves the fixture file byte-identical and the UI renders the denial.
stories.title: Shell and file tool timeout, cancel and output bounds

stories.journey: The security broker authorize call sits on every tool, executor and server tool path with no bypass. Covers the AUD-006 broker-not-wired finding and the executor.rs bash -c bypass.
tests: The executor shell path calls broker authorize before spawn; the direct bash -c bypass is removed.
The server tool path authorizes each call and a denial produces no process or file side effects.
Permission * cannot lift a mandatory human-only grant under any policy version.
A policy version bump invalidates cached approvals; stale approvals are rejected without side effects.
Denied calls emit durable audit events with secrets redacted from logs, history and errors.
stories.title: Broker authorization wired into executor and server tool paths

stories.journey: A real OS sandbox backend confines tool children and closes inherited capabilities before exec on supporting platforms. Covers the AUD-006 sandbox-disclaimer missing finding; a regex or prompt is never advertised as a sandbox.
tests: The Landlock/seccomp backend engages on supported Linux and confines fixture file access to the grant.
File descriptors and capabilities outside the grant are closed before child exec.
An unsupported platform returns explicit BLOCKED, never a silent allow.
A sandbox violation kills the child and reports a typed error with no partial effects.
Repeated sandbox setup/teardown cycles leak no file descriptors or retained mappings.
stories.title: Real OS sandbox backend with inherited-capability close

stories.journey: A real backup module snapshots the live database and restores it, refusing corrupt or stale backups. Covers the AUD-007 missing src/backup_v2.rs finding against an orphaned test file.
tests: A backup of the live database restores to an identical queryable state including history and timestamps.
A corrupted backup fails closed with a typed error and never performs a partial restore.
Restore refuses to overwrite a newer database without an explicit operator flag.
Backups honor the retention quota and prune oldest-first within measured disk bounds.
Concurrent writes during backup yield a consistent snapshot or an explicit retry, never a torn copy.
stories.title: Real backup, restore and corruption detection module

stories.journey: Large and blob history imports run incrementally from a read-only copy and the facade agrees with the migrations table afterwards. Covers the AUD-007 import ponytail and facade-divergence repair items.
tests: A large history imports incrementally from a read-only copy without modifying the source database.
Blob payloads copy out of band within the byte budget instead of the fail-closed ponytail.
Facade and migrations-table state agree after import; any divergence fails the check.
An interrupted import resumes or rolls back to a consistent state with no half-imported sessions.
An oversized blob rejects with an explicit quota error and leaves prior state untouched.
stories.title: Large and blob history import with migration agreement

stories.journey: An LSP client lane runs language servers behind the permission broker with bounded lifecycle. Covers the AUD-009 missing LSP lane finding.
tests: LSP requests route through broker authorization for the workspace root before any server spawn.
An unauthorized workspace root is denied with no spawned server process.
A slow or unresponsive server hits the timeout with bounded queues and no executor starvation.
Cancellation shuts down the server process with no orphan or leaked pipe.
Malformed LSP responses surface typed errors and never panic the host.
stories.title: LSP client lane behind the permission broker

stories.journey: Git operations run as a brokered lane with explicit read versus mutation policy. Covers the AUD-009 missing Git lane finding.
tests: Git mutations outside the authorized root are denied with no repository side effects.
Read-only git commands follow policy while push requires an explicit human-only grant.
Timeout and cancellation kill the child git process and report a stable state.
Ambiguous repository state such as a dirty tree or detached HEAD reports an explicit status.
Git output is bounded and large diffs truncate with an explicit marker.
stories.title: Git lane behind the permission broker

stories.journey: MCP servers spawn only through the permission broker with SSRF and capability guards. Covers the AUD-009 MCP types-only unverified finding.
tests: MCP spawn requires broker approval and a denial spawns no process.
Non-loopback or unauthorized endpoints are blocked as SSRF before connect.
A spawned server inherits only scoped capabilities with inherited handles closed.
A crashed MCP server surfaces a typed error with bounded retry and no silent restart loop.
MCP tool calls carry an approval digest, scope and expiry enforced on each invocation.
stories.title: MCP spawn behind broker with SSRF and capability guards

stories.journey: ACP sessions run live against the bridge with daemon event integration instead of codec-only units. Covers the AUD-009 ACP live-session-wiring repair item.
tests: ACP session start, message, cancel and status round-trip against the live bridge.
Messages sent through ACP appear in the daemon event stream with matching IDs.
An unauthorized session ID is rejected without leaking session existence or content.
Restart during an ACP session recovers a truthful state, never a fabricated completed response.
Message queues stay bounded and a slow peer receives resync or disconnect without blocking others.
stories.title: ACP live session wiring to daemon events

stories.journey: Provider routing, sessions, tools, policy, persistence and events compose into one daemon-owned Rust/Tokio engine shared by every client. Covers audit gap 3 (subsystems are not one engine) and the AUD-010 unwired runtime finding.
tests: A headless submit flows through daemon, execution, events and proxy on one shared engine.
An SDK call and a CLI call observe the same turn ID and state rather than duplicate runtimes.
The workspace proxy enforces session membership on every routed request.
Starting a second engine against the same store fails closed instead of forking state.
Events emitted by the runtime replay identically to late subscribers from a cursor.
stories.title: One daemon-owned application runtime composition

stories.journey: Admission control denies unauthenticated work without side effects and bounds queues, cancellation and restart recovery. Covers the second AUD-010 repair item.
tests: An unauthenticated request is denied with no state change and no side effect.
Cancelling queued work removes it without partial effects or leaked permits.
Restart recovers the queued-versus-committed boundary truthfully with no duplicated effects.
Queue overflow rejects with an explicit backpressure error instead of unbounded growth.
A slow consumer is bounded and resynced without blocking other sessions.
stories.title: Admission control with auth denial and queue bounds

stories.journey: A native application shell renders daemon-owned session, composer, navigation and status state through the owned renderer, replacing line-echo behavior. Covers audit gap 2 (line UI is not OpenTUI) and the AUD-013 frame-parity and live-wiring findings.
tests: Real PTY input changes focus and renders native frames sourced from authenticated daemon state.
Empty, loading, offline and error states are distinguishable and each offers an action.
Tiny and resized terminals never overlap content, panic, or hide the focused control.
A network disconnect renders stale/offline state and never presents fake live data.
The render loop coalesces events, idles when unchanged, and keeps bounded retained history.
stories.title: Native TUI application shell on daemon state

stories.journey: Sharing publishes scoped, expiring, redactable shares with immediate revocation. Covers the first AUD-015 missing share/publish+revoke finding.
tests: Publish creates a scoped share with expiry and revocation invalidates it immediately.
A revoked or expired share is denied without leaking private context.
Published content applies the redaction policy before leaving the daemon.
An unauthorized user cannot enumerate shares or probe their existence.
Publish and revoke append to a bounded audit log with actor, scope and timestamp.
stories.title: Share publish service with revocation and redaction

stories.journey: Account and device pairing gates gateway access with explicit approval while default local use stays offline and account-free. Covers the AUD-015 pairing and tunnel opt-in findings; tunnel transport is not claimed as authentication.
tests: Pairing completes only after explicit user approval binding the device identity.
Tunnel publishing is opt-in and default local use requires no account or network.
No unauthenticated local agent or PTY API is ever published through the gateway.
A revoked device loses access immediately across all sessions and workspaces.
Pairing secrets never appear in logs, exports, transcripts or error messages.
stories.title: Account and device pairing with tunnel opt-in

stories.journey: The mobile client framework, build system, credential store and device-test harness are frozen so MOB-001..006 lanes build against one pinned target. Covers the AUD-016 missing framework-choice finding under COMP-005 authority.
tests: The file pins iOS and Android frameworks, build systems, test runners and versions; unknown fields fail validation.
MOB-001..006 lane plans reference the frozen choice and any deviation fails the check.
Credential storage is fixed to Keychain and Keystore with no plaintext fallback permitted.
Real-device journey requirements reference the frozen harness and signing prerequisites.
Changing the framework requires an explicit re-freeze review and never happens silently.
stories.title: Mobile framework, build and credential-store freeze

stories.journey: Controller acceptance stays pending-integrated, file ownership is enforced by a shared-path lock table, and the lane gate covers discovered lanes. Covers audit gaps 4 and 6 and the AUD-017 repair items; batch refill behavior remains owned by COORD-002.
tests: record_result holds pending-integrated and a fast-forward failure never marks a task accepted.
A failed integration unlocks no dependents and leaves the task out of the ready set.
The shared-path lock table rejects overlapping file edits across distinct tasks.
The lane gate validates discovered lanes or cites the scope document justifying exclusion.
Acceptance requires a post-integration rerun on the exact integrated revision before any flag flips.
stories.title: Controller acceptance, lock table and lane-gate repairs
